extracted.intended_audience: regulated stakeholders, agency staff, attorneys, advocacy groups, and members of the public tracking or participating in HHS rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Producing and interpreting entries in the Department of Health and Human Services semiannual Regulatory Agenda and related Federal Register rulemaking notices, including required metadata, abstracts, timetables, and contact information. Useful for preparing notice-and-comment participation and tracking rule status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Status / Prototype Disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype of a 'Web 2.0' version of the daily Federal Register. It is not an official legal edition of the Federal Register, and does not replace the official print version or the official electronic version on GPO's govinfo.gov. Until the ACFR issues a regulation granting it official legal status, the XML rendition of the daily Federal Register on FederalRegister.gov does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents posted include a link to the corresponding official PDF file on govinfo.gov; those relying on it for legal research should verify results against an official edition of the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Content / PDF Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document posted on the site includes a link to the corresponding official PDF file on govinfo.gov. Use the PDF linked in the document sidebar for the official electronic format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For legal citation or definitive text, consult the official PDF on govinfo.gov rather than the XML/prototype rendition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document Identification Fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register documents include metadata fields such as Agencies, CFR (title/chapters/parts), Document Citation (e.g., 86 FR 41214), Document Number, Document Type (e.g., Proposed Rule), Pages, and Publication Date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These fields appear in the 'Document Details' area and should be present in each Federal Register entry to identify and cite the document correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document Headings (what headings may contain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Document headings vary by document type but may contain: the agency or agencies that issued and signed a document; the number of the CFR title and the number of each part the document amends, proposes to amend, or is directly related to; the agency docket number / agency internal file number; the RIN which identifies each regulatory action listed in the Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Document Drafting Handbook for more details on how headings should be prepared; the reproduced table of contents is a navigational tool and not of substantive legal effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Rule Entry Metadata (Sequence No., Title, RIN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agenda item should present a Sequence No., Title, and Regulation Identifier No. (RIN) to uniquely identify and order the regulatory action within the agency's section of the Agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence and RIN are used to find, cross-reference, and track actions across the Unified Agenda and Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Authority Citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rulemaking abstract includes a 'Legal Authority' line citing the statutory provisions (e.g., 5 U.S.C. 301; 42 U.S.C. 300jj-11) that authorize the agency to promulgate the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate citation of legal authority is required to justify regulatory action and to help readers assess the statutory basis for agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract / Summary Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry must include an abstract that summarizes the purpose, scope, and rationale of the proposed or pending regulatory action (e.g., what the rule would change, why, and the subjects covered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts provide concise context for the public and must describe expected regulatory priorities, statutory context, and the problems the rulemaking addresses; they may note connections to Administration priorities and to Section 610 reviews or other statutory processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable (Action / Date / FR Cite)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each action includes a timetable listing discrete actions (e.g., NPRM, ANPRM, Interim Final Rule, Final Rule, Comment Period End) with associated dates and Federal Register citations (FR Cite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timetables should specify the status and expected timing of each step (and, where applicable, reasons or notes like 'Final Action—Agency Expects No Further Action' or 'Withdrawn'). Timetable entries are used to track comment periods and compliance/readiness dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Analysis Indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rulemaking abstract, the Agenda indicates whether a Regulatory Flexibility Analysis is required (e.g., 'Regulatory Flexibility Analysis Required: Yes' or 'No').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agenda explicitly states this as required information because the Regulatory Flexibility Act requires identification of prospective rulemakings likely to have significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities; this influences the need for analyses and potential outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Contact Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry provides an agency contact (name, title, mailing address, phone number, and email) for further information about the action (e.g., 'Agency Contact: Karuna Seshasai, Executive Secretary... Phone: 202 690-5627, Email: tiffani.redding@hhs.gov').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing a designated contact is required to facilitate public inquiries, submission of comments, and access to supporting materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Stage Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Agenda items are grouped by stage labels such as 'Proposed Rule Stage', 'Final Rule Stage', 'Completed Actions', 'Completed: Reason', 'Long-Term Actions', and 'Completed Actions—Final Action Effective'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage classification communicates current procedural posture of the action and helps readers identify whether and how to participate (e.g., whether a comment period is open).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable Action Types and Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agenda uses a standard set of action types (e.g., ANPRM, NPRM, Interim Final Rule, NPRM Comment Period End, Final Rule, Final Action Effective, Withdrawn) which denote discrete procedural steps in rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should employ these standardized action type terms and pair them with dates and FR citations; reopened comment periods and continuations should be separately listed with their FR cites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Administrative/Programmatic Abstract Details
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts sometimes include programmatic detail such as the problem being addressed, the regulatory approach (e.g., removal of regulatory provisions to align regulation with statute), and whether the rule results from statutory review processes (e.g., 'Rulemaking Resulting From a Section 610 Review').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such explanatory content is expected to help stakeholders understand the rule's purpose and the administrative context (e.g., alignment with statute vs. use of suspension/debarment authorities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to Unified Agenda and RegInfo.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agenda notes that the Department's complete Regulatory Agenda is accessible online at RegInfo.gov and that the RIN identifies actions listed in the Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should cross-reference the Unified Agenda/RIN system so readers can locate more detailed planning information and agency justifications on RegInfo.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of Contents / Enhanced Content as Navigational Tool
rubrics_metrics.description: The page provides an enhanced content Table of Contents processed from headings within legal text for navigation; it repeats headings to form internal navigation links but 'has no substantive legal effect.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TOC and enhanced navigation features improve usability of the online rendition but are explicitly non-substantive; the authoritative content remains the official published document.
